companies.name: Actuals
companies.matchedCompany: Actuals International Pty Ltd (actuals.com) — Melbourne, Australia; AI "Financial Computer" for billing & payroll. Distinct from the unrelated Amsterdam reconciliation startup actuals.io (founded 2016, Peter Engel) and other same-named firms.

founders.name: David Bicknell

founders.name: James (Jimmy) McGill

companies.name: Adora

companies.subtitle: AI platform that maps your live product experience in real time and flags user friction.

Its AI analyses the captured experience to surface friction points, broken flows, and hidden issues, each attached to session replays, so product teams can understand exactly what users experience without manual event tagging. Founded in 2023 by former Canva and Amazon leaders, it launched from private beta with teams at Canva, Notion, Replit, Granola, and Chess.com, and roughly 2,000 companies on its waitlist. Adora is backed by Blackbird Ventures, which led its US$7M (A$9.9M) seed round.

founders.name: Omar Salem

founders.name: Nathan Scully

companies.name: Airwallex

In October 2025 the company surpassed US$1 billion in annualized revenue (up ~90% YoY) and more than US$235 billion in annualized transaction volume. It was one of Australia's earliest tech unicorns and is backed by Blackbird Ventures.

founders.name: Jack Zhang

founders.name: Lucy Liu

founders.name: Max Li

founders.name: Xijing Dai
founders.bio: A University of Melbourne alumnus (also known as Jacob Dai), he co-founded Airwallex and serves as Chief Technology Officer, overseeing the company's engineering and financial infrastructure.

founders.name: Ki-Lok Wong
founders.bio: One of Airwallex's five co-founders, he serves as Principal Architect, contributing to the design of the company's core technical systems.

companies.name: Alloy Index

The platform supports MCAP/ROS file uploads, similarity search across multi-modal data, and automatic scenario clustering across robot fleets, helping robotics companies manage the terabytes of data they generate monthly.

founders.name: Joe Harris
founders.bio: Electrical engineer by training and software builder by craft; began his career as a software developer at Atlassian before joining Blackbird portfolio company Eucalyptus, where he rose to Chief Commercial Officer. He has been fascinated by robotics since childhood and founded Alloy in early 2025.

companies.name: Alloy Robotics

companies.subtitle: Data platform that lets robotics teams search and analyze robot data via natural language
companies.longDescription: Alloy builds the data infrastructure layer for robotics teams. Its platform automatically organizes, searches, and analyzes multimodal robot data — images, time-series sensor data, and system logs from MCAP/ROS files — using natural language queries, turning days-long failure investigations into minute-long queries and letting engineers export findings directly as training datasets. Robots can generate up to a terabyte of data per day, and Alloy positions itself as the deployment/monitoring layer for the "physical AI" revolution. Founded in Sydney in early 2025, it has signed multiple Australian robotics companies as design partners across drone, maritime, defence, and agricultural use cases and is expanding into the US.

founders.name: Joe Harris
founders.bio: Electrical engineer by training and software builder by craft; previously Chief Commercial Officer at Eucalyptus and a software developer at Atlassian, and has advised companies including Halter and Immutable. Founded Alloy in early 2025 after conversations with robotics founders revealed a shared data-management problem.

founders.name: Aaqif Zaman

founders.name: Bernardo (Bernie) Croll
founders.bio: Founding software engineer at Alloy, part of the company's founding team building its robotics data platform.

founders.name: Julia Chen
founders.bio: Part of Alloy's founding team working on fullstack software engineering for the robotics data platform.

companies.name: Alts

Its publications reach 200,000+ investors weekly with deep due diligence and analysis, and members can invest via the actively-managed ALTS 1 Fund (a Reg D fund spanning ~10 alternative asset classes) or through asset-specific instruments offered to its private accredited-investor community, Altea. founders.name: Stefan von Imhof

founders.name: Wyatt Cavalier
founders.bio: Co-founder and CIO of Alts with a background in finance and intelligence analysis, including roles at Barclays Corporate Banking, Booz Allen Hamilton, the Defense Intelligence Agency, and service as a US Army Airborne Ranger. He previously ran the alternative-investing newsletter 'Fractional' before co-founding Alts.

companies.name: Aquila
companies.matchedCompany: Aquila (Aquila Earth) — wireless optical power-beaming startup
companies.subtitle: Building an energy grid of light — wireless, long-range optical power-beaming systems.
companies.longDescription: Aquila (Aquila Earth) is an Australasian deep-tech startup building optical power-beaming technology that transmits electricity wirelessly via high-intensity light/laser beams instead of wires. Its Lightway product family begins with Solais, a system that wirelessly powers drones in flight by beaming optical energy from a ground transmitter to an onboard solar-cell receiver, and scales toward Earth-to-satellite energy networks (Bifrost, Helios, Indra). The long-term mission is to create an "internet of energy" — an infinitely scalable, space-based optical relay network that distributes renewable power from supply to demand anywhere on Earth. The company has attracted interest from customers including the US DARPA and defence partners.

founders.name: Billy Jeremijenko
founders.bio: Software developer and young Australian entrepreneur who co-founded Aquila with a background in maths and statistics and in building complex coordination platforms. He met co-founder Nelson Smith in the Startmate Engineering Fellowship, bonding over a shared interest in space, the environment and lasers. (Blackbird's portfolio page lists his first name as 'Will'.)

founders.name: Nelson Smith
founders.bio: Mechatronics engineer and former Rocket Lab Guidance, Navigation and Control engineer (~3 years building Electron rockets and networked systems), with prior roles at Teknique and ControlVision. He studied Mechatronics and Product Development engineering at the University of Auckland and Massey University and is based in New Zealand.

companies.name: AskNicely
companies.matchedCompany: AskNicely (Ask Nicely Limited) — customer experience / frontline success platform, founded 2014 in Auckland, New Zealand
companies.subtitle: Customer experience and frontline success platform powering real-time NPS feedback for service businesses.
companies.longDescription: AskNicely is a customer experience (CX) software platform that helps service businesses collect real-time customer feedback using the Net Promoter Score (NPS) framework and turn it into action for frontline teams. The platform connects employee experience, customer experience, and revenue growth, delivering personalized coaching, recognition, and motivation to frontline workers based on live feedback. Founded in 2014 in a backyard shed in Auckland, New Zealand by Aaron Ward and John Ballinger, it now serves over 1,300 companies globally with offices in Portland (Oregon), Salt Lake City (Utah), Auckland, and Amsterdam.

founders.name: Aaron Ward
founders.role: Co-founder (founding CEO; later Chief Strategy Officer)
founders.bio: Aaron Ward co-founded AskNicely in 2014, building it from a backyard shed in Auckland into a global CX platform, and served as its long-time CEO before moving into a Chief Strategy Officer role. He has 15+ years in product strategy, previously holding roles at LeapThought NZ, Mighty River Power, and founding lean-startup incubator Red Pill Labs.

founders.name: John Ballinger
founders.bio: John Ballinger co-founded AskNicely with Aaron Ward, originally building the product in his bedroom and then a backyard shed, and led engineering as CTO. He studied Engineering Science at the University of Auckland and later founded reforestation-focused startup Goodsign.

companies.name: Atticus

Founded in Melbourne in 2017 and bootstrapped to profitability, its platform provides an auditable, centralised workflow with version control that reduces manual error and cuts verification time. Its software is used by more than 90% of the Australian corporate legal market, around 30% of the UK's top 30 law firms, and ASX100/FTSE100 companies. In June 2024 it took its first external capital — A$10.84M led by Skip Capital with Blackbird participating.

founders.name: Saul Wakerman

founders.name: Misha Wakerman
founders.bio: A software engineer who previously worked as a Forward Deployed Engineer at Palantir Technologies in Silicon Valley before co-founding Atticus. Brother of co-founder Saul Wakerman.

founders.name: Mitchell Brunton
founders.bio: A software engineer who worked with Misha Wakerman at Palantir Technologies before teaming up with the Wakermans to build Atticus's verification platform.

companies.name: August Robotics
companies.matchedCompany: August Robotics (Hong Kong-based autonomous/mobile robotics company founded by Alex Wyatt; Blackbird portfolio company)
companies.subtitle: Autonomous mobile robots automating dirty, dangerous and dull jobs in construction and industry
companies.longDescription: August Robotics is an international mobile robotics company building application-specific autonomous robots to automate dirty, dangerous and dull jobs across construction and industrial workflows. Its modular platform can ingest project plans, precisely localize robots on-site, plan and execute tasks autonomously, coordinate multiple robots as a fleet, and detect and rectify errors in real time. Its first product, Lionel, is an autonomous floor-marking robot for exhibitions and large indoor spaces (300M+ sq ft marked across five continents); it has since developed autonomous concrete-drilling robots for data-center and hyperscale construction, battle-tested via a partnership with Stanley Black & Decker's DeWalt. In May 2026 it raised a US$30M Series B led by Big Pi Ventures to fund AI development, new products and global expansion.

founders.name: Alex Wyatt
founders.bio: Australian entrepreneur, computer scientist and lawyer (BSc/LLB Melbourne; MPhil/MBA Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar) who founded August Robotics in 2017. He was previously co-founder and CEO of Climate Bridge, a low-carbon project developer in China, and is a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader.

companies.name: Authsignal
companies.matchedCompany: Authsignal (Auckland, NZ consumer authentication / passkeys platform)

companies.longDescription: Authsignal is a B2C consumer authentication and orchestration platform that lets enterprise and mid-market teams deploy passkeys, passwordless login, adaptive/step-up MFA and identity verification through a single API. Its no-code rules engine, fraud controls and user observability tools let teams customize authentication flows across the customer journey to prevent account takeovers while preserving user experience. Customers include MoneyGram, Qualcomm, Air New Zealand, TradeMe, Hnry and First Credit Union. The company was founded by ex-fintech operators frustrated by the complexity and cost of building authentication in-house.

founders.name: Justin Soong
founders.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Authsignal with a deep fintech background across Asia-Pacific, including CTO of ASX-listed Laybuy, work on the Afterpay codebase at Dovetail, and launching P2P lending at Harmoney. He founded Authsignal out of his own frustrations as a CTO with the complexity and cost of implementing authentication, and serves on the Executive Council of Digital Identity NZ.

founders.name: Chris Fisher
founders.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Authsignal. Previously Head of Engineering at telehealth provider Tend, Senior Software Engineer at Pushpay, and held various engineering roles at Vista Group; studied at the University of Cambridge.

companies.name: Baraja

Founded in a Sydney garage by telecommunications engineers Federico Collarte and Cibby Pulikkaseril, the company leverages proven optical-fiber and photonics technology to deliver long-range, software-defined sensing for Level 4 autonomy. Its flagship product, Spectrum HD, was billed as a world-first LiDAR built for automotive-scale connector. Baraja is backed by Blackbird Ventures, Sequoia China, and Main Sequence Ventures (CSIRO Innovation Fund), among others.

founders.name: Federico Collarte
founders.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Baraja, which he started in his Sydney garage in 2016. A telecommunications engineer, he previously held engineering and project-management roles at Cochlear and Motorola before launching the company with co-founder Cibby Pulikkaseril.

founders.name: Cibby Pulikkaseril
founders.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Baraja and the architect of its Spectrum-Scan LiDAR technology. He holds a PhD in heterodyne fiber-optic systems and spent five years at Finisar developing the WaveShaper and WaveAnalyzer products before co-founding Baraja.

companies.name: Baseten
companies.matchedCompany: Baseten (Baseten Labs, Inc.) — AI inference infrastructure platform
companies.subtitle: AI inference platform that deploys and scales ML models in production across multiple clouds.
companies.longDescription: Baseten is a San Francisco-based infrastructure software company that provides a high-scale AI inference platform, helping enterprises deploy and run machine learning models in production without latency, reliability, or cost headaches. Its platform handles the full inference stack — provisioning GPUs across multiple clouds, optimizing model performance, and routing requests to the fastest available compute — and supports both open-source models (Llama, DeepSeek, Whisper) and custom models. Positioned as the "AWS for inference," Baseten serves customers including Cursor, Abridge, Notion, Clay, Mercor, and OpenEvidence. The company has raised $585M to date, most recently a $300M Series E at a $5B valuation (January 2026), with reports of a pending round near an $11B valuation.

founders.name: Pankaj Gupta

The company reports over 2.5 million users across 500,000 companies in 189 countries, including employees at more than 90% of the Fortune 500.

companies.name: Braid

founders.name: Dilani Kahawala

founders.name: Mario Hasanakos
founders.bio: Australian serial founder building the future of teamwork in the AI era. Previously co-founded Australian startups Spriggy (family money app) and Skedulo (mobile workforce management, itself a Blackbird portfolio company).

companies.name: Build Club
companies.matchedCompany: Build Club (buildclub.ai) — AI learning community / e-learning platform founded by Annie Liao, Blackbird & Airtree pre-seed backed
companies.subtitle: The world's most collaborative AI learning community and gig marketplace for builders.
companies.longDescription: Build Club is an AI education community and gig marketplace that helps people learn, build, and get paid for working on real-world AI projects through a "Learn, Build, Earn" model. The platform uses a "bounty" system where businesses submit real problems for members to solve, and partners with AI companies such as NVIDIA, Cohere, Leonardo.AI, and Groq. Its enterprise offering, Solaris, runs AI accelerator/training programs for company teams.

founders.name: Annie Liao

companies.name: Caligra

companies.subtitle: Developer-first computers: a Linux "Workbench" OS and c100 terminal stripped of consumer bloat
companies.longDescription: Caligra is a London-based computer company building "machines for makers" — purpose-built hardware and software for technical professionals such as developers, engineers, scientists and designers. Founded by Australian fintech veterans (the team behind Pin Payments and Up Bank), the company opened pre-orders for its first units in 2025.

founders.bio: Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer of Canva, responsible for operations and fundraising. He co-founded Fusion Books with Melanie Perkins (his partner) prior to Canva, and the couple have pledged to give away the vast majority of their fortune to charity.

founders.name: Cameron Adams

founders.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Carepatron (Ngāti Kahu ki Whangaroa, Ngāi Tūhoe). Spent around seven years at Xero as a senior software developer building products for small businesses; his partner is a medical doctor, which informed his insight into small healthcare practices.

companies.name: Cartesian

It is backed by Google Ventures (GV), Blackbird, Fuel Capital, and numerous celebrity and operator angels.

companies.subtitle: Femtech brand offering a wearable pulse-therapy device for drug-free, instant period pain relief.
companies.longDescription: Ovira is an Australian women's health (femtech) brand founded in 2018 by Alice Williams after her own struggle with endometriosis and debilitating period pain. Its flagship product is a small, discreet wearable TENS/pulse-therapy device that delivers electrical pulses to the abdomen to stop period pain instantly without drugs, designed for the ~88% of women who experience painful menstruation. The company has since expanded into women's-health supplements and built a large direct-to-consumer and social-media following across Australia, the US, Canada and the UK. Backed by Blackbird Ventures, Ovira is listed as an exited company in Blackbird's portfolio.

founders.name: Alice Williams
founders.bio: Alice Williams founded Ovira in 2018 after years of debilitating endometriosis and period pain led her to adapt TENS pulse-therapy technology into a discreet wearable device for drug-free period pain relief. She is the sole founder and CEO and led the company's growth into a global direct-to-consumer women's health brand.

companies.name: Pageload
companies.matchedCompany: Pageload (pageload.io) — Sydney, Australia & Santiago, Chile; transparent web-performance proxy for ecommerce; Blackbird Ventures seed-backed; now closed
companies.subtitle: Transparent proxy that makes ecommerce websites load faster without breaking them.
companies.longDescription: Pageload (pageload.io) was a startup, founded in 2015 with roots in Sydney, Australia, that built a transparent proxy sitting between a website's server and its users, optimizing static assets (JPEG, GIF, PNG, SVG, JS, CSS) in real time via image optimization and CSS/JavaScript minification. It marketed itself as making ecommerce websites load 30-60% faster without breaking the site, improving conversion and revenue while lowering bandwidth and running costs. The company went through Start-Up Chile and built a significant presence in Latin America (with offices/operations in Santiago, Chile), serving large ecommerce retailers including Falabella.com, one of Latin America's largest multinational retailers. Pageload raised an A$300,000 seed round from Blackbird Ventures in 2015 but has since ceased operations (operating status: closed/shutdown).
companies.hqLocation: Sydney, Australia (with operations in Santiago, Chile)

founders.name: Jonathan Lai
founders.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Pageload (2015-2018). He later moved into ecommerce partnerships at Shopify (Senior Manager / Head of ISV Partnerships, APAC; later Lead Program Manager, Partner Operations, Global). Holds a Bachelor of Business from QUT and an MBA in Leadership and Strategy (QUT). Also co-founded Spaces and Inductly.

founders.name: Johan Bergström
founders.bio: Swedish-born serial entrepreneur and software engineer who co-founded and was CTO of Pageload. An early Node.js core contributor and member of its build-infrastructure team; previously co-founded Blogg.se (Scandinavia's largest blogging platform at the time, sold to Aller Media). Later co-founded Habit Global and Emma Cares, and holds a product role at Supabase. Based in Lisbon, Portugal.

companies.name: Proxy
companies.matchedCompany: Proxy Inc. (proxy.com) — universal digital identity signal / mobile access startup, acquired by Ōura
companies.subtitle: Universal digital identity signal for keyless, frictionless access to the physical world.
companies.longDescription: Proxy built a privacy-first "universal identity signal" emitted from a person's smartphone, letting them securely authenticate and interact with doors, devices and services — replacing keys, cards, badges, apps and passwords. It launched with Bluetooth-based keyless office entry used by companies including WeWork, Dropbox and Uber, then expanded toward payments and "wave to pay" on wearables. Co-founded in 2016 by Australians Denis Mars and Simon Ratner, the company was a Y Combinator alum and seed-backed by Blackbird Ventures. It was acquired by smart-ring maker Ōura in an all-equity deal in May 2023.

founders.name: Denis Mars
founders.bio: Australian (Sydney) serial entrepreneur; previously co-founded Bitplay (acquired by Jive Software, 2012) and Modena (acquired 2006). Led Proxy as CEO from its 2016 founding through its 2023 acquisition by Ōura.

founders.name: Simon Ratner
founders.bio: Australian (Sydney) engineer and serial entrepreneur; previously founded video startup Omnisio (acquired by Google/YouTube, 2008) and worked at Jive Software before co-founding Proxy in 2016 as CTO.

companies.name: See-Mode
companies.matchedCompany: See-Mode Technologies Pte. Ltd.
companies.subtitle: AI-augmented ultrasound reporting for thyroid, breast and vascular imaging.
companies.longDescription: See-Mode Technologies builds AI software that automatically analyzes ultrasound images to produce fast, accurate, standardized radiology reports. Originally founded to predict and prevent strokes using computer vision and computational fluid dynamics (its first product AVA automated vascular reporting), the company expanded into FDA-cleared tools that detect and characterize thyroid nodules (TI-RADS) and breast lesions (BI-RADS). Its technology has been shown to reduce ultrasound scan and reporting time by up to 30%. The company was acquired by RadNet (via its DeepHealth subsidiary) in June 2025.

founders.name: Sadaf Monajemi
founders.bio: Dr. Sadaf Monajemi holds a PhD in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the National University of Singapore, specializing in machine learning. She co-founded See-Mode to apply AI to medical-image analysis and was named to MIT Technology Review's Innovators Under 35.

founders.name: Milad Mohammadzadeh
founders.bio: Dr. Milad Mohammadzadeh holds a PhD in Applied Physics and a BSc in Mechanical Engineering from Nanyang Technological University of Singapore, with expertise in mechanics and computational modelling for medical applications. He co-founded See-Mode to bring AI-driven analysis to ultrasound and other medical imaging.

companies.name: Sessions
companies.matchedCompany: Sessions (health coaching startup co-founded by Nick Crocker & Ben Hartney; acquired by MyFitnessPal)
companies.subtitle: Health-coaching platform pairing users with human coaches for 12-week lifestyle change.
companies.longDescription: Sessions was a behavioral-health/coaching startup that paired users with a dedicated human health coach to complete a structured 12-week lifestyle-modification program, with the coach interacting via Skype, email and text to keep members motivated (monthly plans ran roughly $69-$199 depending on coach contact). Founded in 2012 by Australians Nick Crocker and Ben Hartney and incubated out of San Francisco's Rock Health accelerator, it reported roughly 90% program-completion rates, far above industry engagement norms. It raised under $1M from SV Angel, Collaborative Fund, Blackbird Ventures and Joshua Kushner (Thrive Capital). MyFitnessPal acquired Sessions in February 2014 — MyFitnessPal's first acquisition — with the founders and team joining to build coaching into MyFitnessPal's 50M+ user base; the standalone Sessions coaching service was subsequently wound down.

founders.name: Nick Crocker
founders.bio: Australian entrepreneur who co-founded Sessions (acquired by MyFitnessPal, where he became a Product Manager) and previously co-founded We Are Hunted (acquired by Twitter); he was also a product manager at Boxee. He is now a General Partner at Blackbird Ventures running its Melbourne office, and holds Political Science and Law degrees from the University of Queensland.

founders.name: Ben Hartney
founders.bio: Australian product leader who co-founded Sessions, a software company to help people live better, more active lives, which was acquired by MyFitnessPal. He later worked in product management roles and is now a Product Manager at Google; he studied at the University of Queensland.

companies.name: Shape Analytics
companies.matchedCompany: Shape Analytics (also branded "Shape"), the people analytics startup co-founded by Tuhin Srivastava and Philip Howes, acquired by Reflektive in 2018
companies.subtitle: People analytics platform unifying HR data into reporting, insights, and predictions
companies.longDescription: Shape Analytics (branded "Shape") built a people analytics platform that brought together employee data from disparate sources across an organization and delivered comprehensive reporting, insights, and predictions without requiring a dedicated data science team. Founded in 2015 by Tuhin Srivastava and Philip Howes, it was backed by Blackbird Ventures, Lowercase Capital, and Caffeinated Capital, raising roughly $1.7M. In June 2018 it was acquired by performance-management company Reflektive, where its technology was integrated as "Reflektive Analytics." The founders later went on to co-found AI infrastructure company Baseten in 2019.

founders.name: Tuhin Srivastava
founders.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Shape Analytics (2015-2019). Previously an investment banker at Macquarie Group and a data scientist/ML engineer at Skulpt and Gumroad; later co-founded and became CEO of AI infrastructure company Baseten in 2019.

founders.name: Philip Howes
founders.bio: Co-founder of Shape Analytics. Holds a PhD in Mathematics from the University of Sydney and previously worked as a machine learning engineer at Gumroad; later co-founded and became Chief Scientist of AI infrastructure company Baseten in 2019.

companies.name: Sunroom
companies.matchedCompany: Sunroom (sunroom.so) — creator platform for women and non-binary creators, co-founded by Lucy Mort and Michelle Battersby; Blackbird Ventures portfolio company, acquired by Fanfix in 2025
companies.subtitle: Creator monetization platform empowering women and non-binary creators
companies.longDescription: Sunroom was a subscription-based creator platform built as a safer, women- and non-binary-centered alternative to mainstream social media like Instagram, TikTok and OnlyFans. Creators monetized through monthly subscriptions, tips and in-app reactions, with features such as proprietary "SunBlock" anti-screenshot technology, human-led content moderation, and reduced fees for Black, Indigenous and Hispanic creators. Founded by ex-Hinge design director Lucy Mort and ex-Bumble marketing director Michelle Battersby, the app launched on iOS in February 2022 and onboarded tens of thousands of creators. It was acquired by creator platform Fanfix in 2025, with creators and content migrating over to Fanfix.

founders.name: Lucy Mort
founders.bio: Australian designer and product leader who previously served as Director of Design at Hinge (2015-2019). She co-founded Sunroom as CEO and lead designer, building an app aimed at reducing the stigmas and restrictions women and non-binary people face when monetizing themselves online. She holds a Bachelor of Design from UNSW.

founders.name: Michelle Battersby
founders.bio: Australian marketing executive who built and led Bumble's marketing across APAC (Country Lead Australia, then Director APAC Marketing) before co-founding Sunroom as Chief Marketing Officer. She studied a Bachelor of Arts in Sociology and Management at the University of Sydney.

founders.name: Ellie Day
founders.bio: Technical co-founder of Sunroom with an engineering background, identified as the company's CTO; cited in interviews as the third co-founder who joined Mort and Battersby at the company's founding.

companies.name: Zoox
companies.matchedCompany: Zoox, Inc. (autonomous robotaxi company, Foster City, CA; acquired by Amazon)
companies.subtitle: Purpose-built autonomous, electric robotaxi company creating mobility-as-a-service.
companies.longDescription: Zoox is an autonomous-vehicle company founded in 2014 that designs purpose-built, symmetrical, bi-directional battery-electric robotaxis from the ground up, rather than retrofitting conventional cars, to deliver an autonomous ride-hailing (mobility-as-a-service) experience. Co-founded by Australian artist-designer Tim Kentley-Klay and Stanford self-driving researcher Dr. Jesse Levinson, it became one of the most prominent and well-capitalized startups in the robotaxi space, reaching a $3.2B valuation. Amazon acquired Zoox in June 2020 for over $1.2 billion, operating it as a wholly owned subsidiary; the company has since launched public robotaxi services in Las Vegas and San Francisco. Blackbird Ventures was Zoox's first investor, backing the 2014 seed round and later participating in the Series B.

founders.name: Tim Kentley-Klay
founders.bio: Australian artist-designer and former online-advertising entrepreneur who co-founded Zoox in 2014 and led it as CEO until 2018, building it to a $3.2B valuation; later co-founded HYPR, an AI robotics company. Named 'Advance Global Australian' in 2020.

founders.name: Jesse Levinson
founders.bio: Co-founder and CTO of Zoox, responsible for its software, AI, computing and sensing platforms. He earned a Computer Science PhD at Stanford under Sebastian Thrun, developing algorithms for Stanford's 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge entry, and is the son of Apple chairman Arthur D. Levinson.

companies.name: Articore
companies.matchedCompany: Articore Group Limited (formerly Redbubble Limited / Redbubble Group), ASX: ATG
companies.subtitle: Global print-on-demand marketplaces (Redbubble & TeePublic) connecting independent artists with buyers
companies.longDescription: Articore Group Limited (formerly Redbubble Limited / Redbubble Group) owns and operates the global print-on-demand creator marketplaces Redbubble.com and TeePublic.com, where independent artists upload original designs that customers buy on apparel, stationery, wall art, homewares and other everyday products. Founded in Melbourne in 2006, the company listed on the ASX in May 2016 and acquired US-based TeePublic in 2018. It rebranded from Redbubble to Articore Group in late 2023 and trades on the ASX under ticker ATG.

founders.name: Martin Hosking
founders.role: Co-founder; former Executive Chair, CEO and Non-Executive Director (departed June 2025)
founders.bio: Martin Hosking co-founded Redbubble in 2006 and served as its long-time CEO and chair, leading the company through its 2016 ASX IPO; he returned as CEO of Articore in 2023 before departing in June 2025. He was previously chair of construction-software firm Aconex.

founders.name: Peter Styles
founders.role: Co-founder (no longer involved with the company)
founders.bio: Peter (Pete) Styles co-founded Redbubble in 2006 alongside Martin Hosking and Paul Vanzella, helping conceive the artist-focused marketplace. He is no longer involved with the company.

founders.name: Paul Vanzella
founders.role: Co-founder (subsequently focused on his own design studio)
founders.bio: Paul Vanzella co-founded Redbubble in 2006 with Martin Hosking and Peter Styles, contributing design expertise to the early platform. He later focused primarily on his own boutique design studio rather than Redbubble's operations.

companies.name: Azonic
companies.matchedCompany: Azonic (azonic.ai) — Auckland, New Zealand criminal intelligence platform; legal entity AZONIC LIMITED (NZ company no. 9415837)
companies.subtitle: Unified, agentic criminal intelligence platform for law enforcement and intelligence agencies
companies.longDescription: Azonic is a New Zealand startup building a unified, agentic intelligence platform for law enforcement and intelligence agencies investigating online crime. It consolidates fragmented OSINT tools, proprietary databases, analytical workflows, and internal systems into a single platform where human analysts and autonomous AI agents can run hundreds of concurrent investigations in parallel. The platform proactively surfaces emerging threats through continuous monitoring of online platforms before harm occurs. The company was incorporated as Azonic Limited in Auckland in March 2026. Co-founder and CEO Caden Scott also founded the non-profit International Online Crime Coordination Center (IOC3), which connects victims, online platforms, analysts and law enforcement agencies such as the DIA, FBI and Interpol. Co-founder and CTO Thomas Holdom leads engineering, with a background building AI infrastructure and production agentic systems.

founders.name: Caden Scott
founders.bio: Caden Scott started programming at age 10 building games on Roblox and went on to study Innovation and Entrepreneurship at the University of Auckland. He is co-founder and CEO of Azonic and also Executive Director of the International Online Crime Coordination Center (IOC3), a non-profit that connects victims, platforms, analysts and law enforcement agencies including the DIA, FBI and Interpol. He is listed as a director of Azonic Limited (registered name Caden Flynn Scott).

founders.name: Thomas Holdom
founders.bio: Thomas Holdom is co-founder and CTO of Azonic, leading engineering. He has a background building AI infrastructure and production-ready agentic systems for enterprises and startups. He is listed as a director of Azonic Limited (registered name Thomas Maurice Holdom).

companies.name: Predictive Text Labs
companies.matchedCompany: Predictive Text Labs (PTL, ptl.inc)
companies.subtitle: Temporal AI startup building models that forecast the future to power decisions.
companies.longDescription: Predictive Text Labs builds AI that predicts the future, arguing that when leaders ask "what should I do?" they want an actionable answer rooted in a prediction, not another chart. The company contends that while LLMs summarise the past brilliantly, reasoning to forecast events is fundamentally different from predicting the next token, so it focuses on temporal reasoning as the core primitive that turns LLMs from search engines into decision-making partners. It is an early-stage, largely stealth venture led by co-CEOs Chris Bach (Netlify co-founder) and Alex Pan (Storipress founder, Forbes 30 Under 30), with CTO Athon Millane and PhD researchers in time-series (Ming Jin, Griffith University) and graph methods (Andy Huang, Oxford). The founding team is Australian-rooted and based in Sydney, and the company is backed by Blackbird Ventures.

founders.name: Chris Bach
founders.bio: Serial entrepreneur and co-founder of Netlify, the web platform powering 90M+ sites, where he helped pioneer the Jamstack movement and the decoupled web. Now Co-CEO of Predictive Text Labs.

founders.name: Alex Pan
founders.bio: Machine-learning engineer and product/design leader, UNSW-educated and a Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree. He previously founded Storipress (an all-in-one publisher CMS) and authored an early synthetic benchmark for verifiable mixed-logic reasoning and state management. Co-CEO of Predictive Text Labs, based in Sydney.

founders.name: Athon Millane
founders.bio: Data scientist who built DLFinLab, a deep-learning algorithmic-trading system used by quant funds, and previously ML/Research Lead at Max Kelsen. Australia-based technologist (also founder/CTO of MedNotes.ai) serving as CTO of Predictive Text Labs.

companies.name: Ao Air
companies.matchedCompany: Aō Air (formerly O2O2) — New Zealand respiratory-protection startup, maker of the ATMOS faceware; Blackbird Ventures' first NZ-fund investment
companies.subtitle: Maker of ATMOS "faceware" — a wearable, positive-pressure air-filtration respirator
companies.longDescription: Aō Air (formerly known as O2O2) is a New Zealand-founded respiratory-protection company building the next generation of personal air filtration to replace cloth and N95 masks. Its flagship product, the ATMOS, is a transparent wearable "faceware" band that uses dual induction fans to draw air through proprietary nanofibre filters, creating a positive-pressure air seal that captures over 98% of PM2.5 particulate matter — claimed in independent testing (Auckland University of Technology) to offer up to 50x better protection than market-leading respirators. The company was the inaugural investment from Blackbird Ventures' New Zealand fund and also passed through accelerators including SOSV/HAX, URBAN-X and Dassault's 3DEXPERIENCE Lab. It is now recorded as written off in Blackbird's portfolio.

founders.name: Dan Bowden
founders.bio: Dan (Daniel) Bowden led Aō Air's commercialisation, bringing a background investing across UK businesses spanning healthcare, hotels and petrol stations, and championing a customer- and design-centric approach to respiratory products.

founders.name: Jeremy Mauger
founders.bio: A University of Auckland-trained chemist who spent much of his career building props in the film industry, Jeremy Mauger developed the ATMOS device and led manufacturing, testing, design and filter chemistry. He later served as Co-CEO of the company.

founders.name: Ilya Vensky
founders.bio: Ilya Vensky brought consumer-marketing expertise and led the company's branding; having introduced Western brands to China, he was driven to tackle air quality after pollution-related health issues forced his family to leave the country.

companies.name: Bardee
companies.matchedCompany: Bardee (Bardee Pty Ltd) — Melbourne, Australia black soldier fly food-waste-to-protein/fertiliser agtech
companies.subtitle: Transforms food waste into insect protein and fertiliser using black soldier fly larvae.
companies.longDescription: Bardee is a Melbourne-based agtech / climate-tech company founded in 2019 that uses black soldier fly larvae to transform pre- and post-consumer food waste into high-value products such as insect protein for livestock and pet feed, plus organic fertiliser. Founders Phoebe Gardner and Alex Arnold began the venture by chopping discarded tuna heads in a university car park to feed insects in a benchtop-scale lab, later building a ~2,500sqm vertical-farming facility in Melbourne's northwest (Sunshine). The company raised a $5M seed round led by Blackbird Ventures in late 2021, but struggled to raise further capital, laid off around 30 staff in May 2023, and its former parent company was handed to liquidators in 2024.

founders.name: Phoebe Gardner
founders.bio: Architect by training who co-founded Bardee in 2019 and serves as CEO, leading the company's mission to reshape the global food system by upcycling food waste with insects.

founders.name: Alex Arnold
founders.bio: Entomologist and soil scientist who co-founded Bardee in 2019 and serves as CTO, developing the black soldier fly larvae bioconversion technology that turns food waste into protein and fertiliser.

companies.name: Bellish
companies.matchedCompany: Bellish (bellish.co) — Australian knitting/crochet pattern-generator app founded by Megan Elizabeth, Blackbird Ventures portfolio company
companies.subtitle: Free app with a "pattern engine" that generates custom knitting and crochet patterns in minutes.
companies.longDescription: Bellish was an Australian consumer-tech startup that built a free mobile app and digital toolset to make designing knitting and crochet patterns accessible to anyone, no design skills required. Its proprietary "pattern engine" let users pick a base, silhouette, size, yarn and embellishments to instantly generate an original sweater or beanie pattern with interactive instructions, row counters and stitch checkpoints — eliminating the 50+ hours an experienced designer normally spends per pattern. The app launched in February 2020 and grew rapidly during COVID-19 lockdowns, reaching 60,000+ Apple downloads (about 80% in North America) and 115,000+ user-created designs by June 2020. The company was later wound down and is listed as written off / deadpooled.

founders.name: Megan Elizabeth
founders.bio: A lifelong knitter taught by her mother, grandmother and aunt, Megan Elizabeth founded Bellish after being frustrated by how hard it was to find or design the exact knitting pattern she wanted; she set out to make pattern design free and accessible to everyone through software.

companies.name: Black.ai
companies.matchedCompany: black.ai (Black Innovation Pty Ltd), Melbourne, Australia — computer-vision autonomous retail / spatial-AI startup backed by Blackbird Ventures
companies.subtitle: Computer-vision platform using ceiling 3D sensors to map customer behaviour in physical retail spaces.
companies.longDescription: Black.ai built an autonomous retail platform that mapped and monitored physical stores in real time using a small number of discreet ceiling-mounted 3D depth sensors. The system maintained a virtual "cart" for each shopper, detecting product pickup and put-down events (even for visually similar fresh produce) to reduce self-checkout loss and surface in-store customer insights. The company positioned itself more broadly as an AI startup focused on automation in real spaces, with applications extending into healthcare and mining (monitoring patient vital signs and tracking staff and heavy machinery). Backed by Blackbird Ventures, the company is recorded as Written Off in Blackbird's portfolio.

founders.name: Keaton Okkonen
founders.bio: Co-founder and CEO of Black.ai with a software engineering and cybersecurity background; previously a freelance security researcher (bug bounties for Yahoo, Citrix, Coinbase, LinkedIn) and a 2016 RMIT University computer science graduate. He met his co-founders at hackathons and the company came out of the Startmate 2017 accelerator.

founders.name: Sebastien Collier
founders.bio: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of Black.ai, leading the company's technical and engineering development of its 3D-sensor computer-vision platform.

founders.name: Karthik Rajgopal Laxmi Naarayanan
founders.bio: Co-founder and Director of Research at Black.ai. Originally from southern India (born in Kochi, raised in Chennai), he holds a bachelor's and master's in computer science from Melbourne and worked as a database/full-stack/front-end and machine-learning engineer; he met co-founders Keaton and Sebastien at hackathons.

companies.name: Carted
companies.matchedCompany: Carted (Australian universal commerce API / shopping wishlist startup, founded by Holly Cardew & Mike Angell, Blackbird-backed)
companies.subtitle: Universal commerce API turning content & social platforms into shoppable storefronts.
companies.longDescription: Carted built a "universal commerce API" that let developers, creators and content platforms connect to millions of merchants and billions of products through a single connector, enabling direct, in-context checkout instead of clunky redirects and affiliate links. It later pivoted toward a consumer "ultimate wishlist" shopping app that let shoppers save products from across the web and get notified when items went on sale or were restocked. Backed by one of Australia's largest-ever seed rounds (A$13M in 2021, led by Blackbird), the company struggled to reach scale as social platforms added native commerce and AI/agentic shopping reshaped the market. Carted wound down operations on 22 October 2025.

founders.name: Holly Cardew
founders.bio: Australian entrepreneur who previously founded Pixc, an image-editing platform for e-commerce sellers. She co-founded Carted in 2020 to build a universal commerce API and led the company through its record seed round and 2025 wind-down.

founders.name: Mike Angell
founders.bio: Self-taught engineer who previously worked at Shopify and served as COO of Australian streetwear retailer Culture Kings. He co-founded Carted but departed within months of the seed round (later joining NFT marketplace Fractal) and relinquished his vested equity stake.

companies.name: EnergyBank
companies.matchedCompany: EnergyBank Limited (energybank.nz) — Auckland, New Zealand gravity/ocean energy-storage startup, Blackbird seed portfolio company
companies.subtitle: Ocean-based gravity battery for grid-scale, long-duration renewable energy storage.
companies.longDescription: EnergyBank was a New Zealand deep-tech startup developing a novel gravity-based, medium and long-duration energy storage system for the offshore wind and renewables market. Its technology stores energy by raising and lowering multiple thousand-tonne masses (iron-ore aggregate) between the ocean floor and surface over vertical distances of 4-8km, connected to the grid via undersea cable. The company positioned this as a lower-cost, more scalable and more environmentally friendly alternative to pumped-hydro and lithium-ion batteries, requiring no land and carrying minimal accident risk. Blackbird led an oversubscribed seed round in 2021.

founders.name: Tim Hawkey
founders.bio: University of Auckland mechanical-engineering graduate and Velocity entrepreneurship-program alumnus from New Plymouth, NZ. Grew up immersed in the energy sector through his father, who built and managed power stations, and founded EnergyBank in 2019 after living in San Francisco.

founders.name: Rhys Foster
founders.bio: A roughly 20-year (10+ year) veteran of the US renewables and energy-storage sector who pioneered grid-connected, utility-scale lithium-ion battery technology at A123 and led sales, engineering and business development at NEC before joining EnergyBank.

founders.name: Jordan Hooper
founders.bio: Brought a background in offshore oil-and-gas construction to the founding team; met Tim Hawkey at a party after being laid off from the oil-and-gas industry during the pandemic.

companies.name: Forte
companies.matchedCompany: Forte (Financing Of Return To Employment) / Forte Global, Inc.
companies.subtitle: Finances reskilling at no cost via investor returns tied to future tax revenue.
companies.longDescription: Forte (Financing Of Return To Employment) is an education-finance platform that lets investors pay for the vocational reskilling of individuals who would otherwise pay little or no tax. As trainees gain employment and earn higher incomes, governments pass back to investors an agreed portion of the resulting increase in income-tax revenue for a set period, meaning training is free for participants and costless upfront for governments. The mechanism was invented by founder Dr. Nat Ware during his PhD on education finance at Oxford, and Forte has run programs in markets including Australia, Colombia, Costa Rica and Puerto Rico.

founders.name: Dr. Nat Ware
founders.bio: Australian social-impact economist, entrepreneur and Rhodes Scholar who invented the Forte (Financing Of Return To Employment) mechanism during his PhD on education finance at Oxford. Previously founded 180 Degrees Consulting, the world's largest consultancy for nonprofits and social enterprises, and is a Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree.

companies.name: Heuros
companies.matchedCompany: Heuros (Brisbane-based cellular agriculture / cultivated meat biotech developing GM-free growth factors; Blackbird Ventures portfolio company)
companies.subtitle: Cellular-agriculture biotech making GM-free, serum-free growth media for cultivated (clean) meat.
companies.longDescription: Heuros is an Australian cellular-agriculture startup developing the growth factors and culture media needed to grow muscle cells for cultivated (clean) meat without foetal bovine serum (FBS), blood products, genetic modification, recombinant proteins, hormones or antibiotics. Operating primarily as a B2B supplier, it aimed to sell its low-cost, GM-free media to other cultivated-meat companies worldwide while developing its own consumer products. Backed by Blackbird Ventures and the ProVeg Incubator, the company was ultimately written off.

founders.name: Nick Beaumont
founders.bio: Dr. Nick (N.J.) Beaumont is the founder of Heuros and spent more than 20 years researching biochemistry and molecular biology in universities and medical schools before starting the company. He drove the development of Heuros' GM-free, serum-free growth media for cultivated meat.

founders.name: Jordan Sosnowski
founders.bio: Jordan 'Jordy' Sosnowski is a co-founder of Heuros with a legal and animal-advocacy background, having served as Advocacy Director at Action for Dolphins. She holds a Juris Doctor and Master of Laws from Monash University and was an Associate Fellow at the Oxford Centre for Animal Ethics.
founders.location: Byron Bay, New South Wales, Australia

companies.name: Hey
companies.matchedCompany: Hey You (formed from the 2014 merger of Posse and Beat the Q; café order-ahead & mobile payments platform)
companies.subtitle: Australia's leading order-ahead and mobile payments app for cafes and restaurants.
companies.longDescription: Hey You was an Australian mobile order-ahead and payments platform that let consumers order and pay ahead at cafes and restaurants to skip the queue. It was formed in 2014 from the merger of Rebekah Campbell's recommendation app Posse with Adam Theobald's cafe-ordering startup Beat the Q (plus E-Coffee Card), and rebranded to "Hey You" in 2015. At its peak it was Australia's largest cafe-focused mobile payments platform, with over a million users and tens of millions of orders. In December 2022 the business merged with last-mile courier Drive Yello to form 4You Innovation; Blackbird's investment in the company was ultimately written off.

founders.name: Rebekah Campbell
founders.bio: Australian serial entrepreneur and author who founded the recommendation app Posse (2010) and led its 2014 merger with Beat the Q to create Hey You, serving as co-CEO. She later co-founded Zambesi and wrote the memoir '138 Dates'.

founders.name: Adam Theobald
founders.role: Co-Founder & Co-CEO (founder of Beat the Q)
founders.bio: Australian entrepreneur who founded the cafe order-ahead startup Beat the Q in 2011 and co-founded Hey You via the 2014 merger, serving as co-CEO. He later founded hospitality ordering platform Ordermentum.

companies.name: HIVERY
companies.matchedCompany: HIVERY (Red Analytics Pty Ltd), Sydney-based AI retail category management startup spun out of CSIRO's Data61
companies.subtitle: AI-driven retail category management and shelf/assortment optimization for CPGs and retailers
companies.longDescription: HIVERY was an Australian artificial intelligence company that helped consumer packaged goods companies and retailers maximize their return on retail space investment through machine learning and operations research.
